key_insight: REFLEX uses Jev as a fast typed decision layer to avoid many expensive LLM calls while preserving task success through selective fallback to a stronger model.
engineering_relevance: For LLM agents, this suggests a practical control strategy that can cut inference cost and latency when decisions are mostly bounded and confidence can be reliably estimated.
method: Jev handles fast, typed decisions and routes low-confidence or generative cases to a strong LLM.
The system was tested on a frozen 100-task benchmark with controlled fallback comparisons.
Interventions examined when selective control works best, especially around action-set size and authorization-boundary edge cases.
evidence_signal: On a 100-task benchmark, REFLEX achieved 95% success while reducing strong-model calls by 72.7%, with similar savings across three fallback families.
watch_item: Benefits appear limited when ordinary routing is already highly accurate, so the added control layer may not justify complexity in all deployments.
paper_title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
